facts.statement: Longusunguis is an extinct enantiornithean dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Liaoning Province in northeastern China.
facts.quote: Longusunguis is an extinct genus of bohaiornithid enantiornithean dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous of Liaoning Province, northeastern China.

facts.statement: The genus Longusunguis was first described and named by Min Wang, Zhong-He Zhou, Jingmai K. O'Connor, and Nikita V. Zelenkov in 2014.
facts.quote: Longusunguis was first described and named by Min Wang, Zhong-He Zhou, Jingmai K. O'Connor and Nikita V. Zelenkov in 2014

facts.statement: The generic name Longusunguis means "long claw" in Latin, referring to the animal's distinctly elongated foot claws.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Latin words longus, meaning "long", and unguis, meaning "claw", in reference to the distinctly elongated pedal unguals

facts.statement: The species name kurochkini honors the late paleontologist Evgeny Kurochkin for his work on fossil birds.
facts.quote: The specific name, kurochkini, honors the late Prof. Evgeny Kurochkin, a prominent paleontologist, for his contributions to the study of fossil birds.

facts.statement: Longusunguis is known only from a single complete and articulated skeleton and skull, the holotype IVPP V 17964.
facts.quote: Longusunguis is known solely from the holotype IVPP V 17964, a complete and articulated skeleton and skull.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected near Lamadong Town in Liaoning Province from the Jiufotang Formation, dating to approximately 120.3 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: IVPP V 17964 was collected at deposits near the Lamadong Town, Jianchang County of the Liaoning Province, from the Jiufotang Formation, dated to the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 120.3 million years ago.

facts.statement: Longusunguis possesses a unique accessory fenestra on the jugal process of its maxilla.
facts.quote: The maxilla of Longusunguis possesses an accessory fenestra on the jugal process.

facts.statement: The lateral margin of the coracoid in Longusunguis is more convex than in other bohaiornithids.
facts.quote: In Longusunguis, the lateral margin of the coracoid is more convex than in other bohaiornithids.

facts.statement: The acromion process in Longusunguis projects strongly dorsally, distinguishing it from the straight process found in Parabohaiornis.
facts.quote: In Longusunguis, the acromion process is strongly projecting dorsally (more than in Sulcavis), whereas in Parabohaiornis this process is straight, and is parallel to the scapular shaft.

facts.statement: In Longusunguis, the pygostyle is longer than the tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: Finally, its pygostyle is longer than the tarsometatarsus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen represents a subadult individual, indicated by the lack of fusion in compound bones like the carpometacarpus and tarsometatarsus.
facts.quote: The holotype of Longusunguis came from a subadult individual, as evident by the absence of fusion in some compound bones, such as the carpometacarpus, tibiotarsus and tarsometatarsus.

facts.statement: Longusunguis lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
